content.text: {"answer": 2, "reduction": 2, "lower_bound": 2, "upper_bound": 2, "lower_bound_mechanism": "cheap-witness descent: minimal transversal containing prime q>a_1 yields geometric shrinking d_{Q'} < (a_1/q) d_Q, contradiction; hence all member primes <= a_1", "upper_bound_mechanism": "S = {m >= a_1 : some d_Q | m} with d_Q | M = prod_{p<=a_1} p; each length-M block holds exactly T terms, shift bijection gives a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n>=1", "wrong_answer_stated": false, "notes": "Complete and rigorous: Lemmas 1-3 (self-consistency plus greedy downward coprime witness), Lemma 4 minimal-transversal characterization, Lemma 5 pairwise intersection, Lemma 6/7 descent proving no member prime exceeds a_1, Lemma 8 finiteness, and a clean block-counting argument giving periodicity from n=1, not merely eventually."}
